summary_html: The child is **removed from the home** and placed in foster care under court order or emergency authority. Federal statutes tie funding to safety findings, judicial oversight, and permanency planning.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Jackson E.
key_cases.holding: The court held that foster parents, including one who was also the child's maternal grandmother, lack standing to appeal a juvenile court order changing the child's placement, and dismissed the appeal for lack of jurisdiction.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes who may and may not contest a foster placement decision on appeal in Nebraska.
key_cases.quote: As foster parents, Erin and Paul do not have standing to appeal the change in Jackson's placement.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Jordon B.
key_cases.holding: The court held that foster parents have a statutory right to participate in review hearings but no right to intervene as parties or to appeal a placement order, and that the adult adoptive relative was not a 'sibling' entitled to intervene.
key_cases.relevance: It is the most recent Nebraska Supreme Court statement of foster parents' procedural role in placement decisions.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that as foster parents, the Todds did not have the right to intervene as parties and did not have the right to appeal the juvenile court's placement order.

key_cases.case_name: Jill B. & Travis B. v. State
key_cases.holding: The court held that foster and adoptive parents' claims that the State failed to disclose the placed child's sexual history are barred by the State Tort Claims Act's misrepresentation exception, including any theory framed as an independent operational duty to disclose or warn.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the legal consequence in Nebraska of an agency's failure to tell a foster home about a placed child's known risk history.
key_cases.quote: Any operational duty to disclose information or to warn the parents about K.D.M.'s sexual history is subsumed by the misrepresentation exception.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Paxton H.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the juvenile court did not err in ordering DHHS to arrange and pay for the child's placement and services at an out-of-state psychiatric residential treatment facility, and that such a cost order is a final, appealable order.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms the juvenile court's authority over the agency's placement decisions, including out-of-state residential placements.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the juvenile court did not err in ordering DHHS to arrange and pay for Paxton to receive services at KidsTLC.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Enyce J. & Eternity M.
key_cases.holding: The court held that foster parents have no legal or equitable right, title, or interest in the subject matter of a juvenile case, so they lack standing to appeal an order changing the child's placement and are not entitled to intervene as of right, and it disapproved In re Interest of Jorius G. & Cheralee G. and In re Interest of Montana S. to the extent they were inconsistent.
key_cases.relevance: This is the foundational Nebraska holding, applied without restatement in In re Interest of Jackson E. and In re Interest of Jordon B., that the statutory role § 43-1314 gives foster parents in the proceeding confers no interest supporting an appeal of a placement decision.
key_cases.quote: Mark and Roberta did not have a right, title, or interest in the subject matter of the controversy that gave them standing
